title: Assemble a dispatch packet with a form at the end
purpose: Bundle the three shipping pages and the handover form into one attachment so the recipient can print them in order.
step: Put dispatch.pdf first and handover.pdf last. Look at the thumbnails before merging.
check: Open the four-page result. Packing list should be first and Dispatch handover should be last.

title: Separate a receipt from a dispatch packet
purpose: Send the dispatch receipt separately while keeping the packing list and pickup instructions together.
step: Create a range for pages 1–2 and another for page 3, then split the packet.
check: Open both parts. The receipt should contain DEMO-482 and the pickup instructions should appear only in the two-page part.

title: Compress a scanned pickup note for an attachment
purpose: Reduce the weight of an image-based note while keeping its short stock code legible.
step: Start with a moderate compression setting. Compare the new size with the source before deciding which copy to keep.
check: Zoom in on Code A17 and Twelve notebooks. A smaller file is useful only if both lines remain readable.

title: Recover a dispatch PDF with a damaged file index
purpose: A PDF can contain intact pages even when its final index points to the wrong byte. This practice file has that specific fault.
step: Open the damaged copy in Repair PDF and run its check. Use the recovery option appropriate to the reported condition.
check: Compare the recovered copy against the expected three pages. On the final page look for DEMO-482.

title: Export one receipt page as a JPG
purpose: Make a picture of the receipt for a system that accepts images. The receipt is the third page of the practice packet.
step: Choose the page-image mode, select page 3 and export a JPG at a resolution high enough to read the reference.
check: Open the image by itself. It should show Dispatch receipt and DEMO-482, with no packing-list page.

title: Put two shelf-label images on separate PDF pages
purpose: Make a print packet from two source images without stretching their rectangular artwork.
step: Select the JPG and PNG together. Give each image its own page and inspect the margins in the preview.
check: The finished document should contain two pages. The circle on each label should still look round.

title: Rotate one page in a mixed-orientation packet
purpose: Correct a single sheet without rotating the rest of the packet. The practice target is the middle page.
step: Select only page 2 and rotate it by one quarter turn. Leave the other two thumbnails in their original orientation.
check: Reopen the output and compare pages 1 and 3 against the source. Only Pickup instructions should have turned.

title: Number a three-page packet starting at 10
purpose: Continue an existing binder’s numbering when a new section begins on page ten.
step: Set the first printed number to 10 and select a footer position clear of the existing practice-file caption.
check: Check the three new labels in sequence. The first should read 10 and the last should read 12.

title: Remove an internal sheet before sending a packet
purpose: Send the packing list and receipt without the internal pickup instructions.
step: Mark the second page for deletion. Check the two retained thumbnails before processing.
check: The first remaining page should say Packing list and the second Dispatch receipt. Reopen the copy before sending it.

title: Save the receipt from a multipage PDF
purpose: Give a colleague just the signed-off receipt while keeping the full source packet for your records.
step: Select page 3 as the only page to extract. Leave the source file in place.
check: Open the extracted file and verify that it has one page with the reference DEMO-482.

title: Put pickup instructions at the front of a packet
purpose: Create a driver’s copy with the first action on the first page.
step: Move the Pickup instructions thumbnail ahead of Packing list and leave Dispatch receipt last.
check: Read the exported pages in order. They should start with the pickup window and end with the reference code.

title: Make a PDF scan from a photographed dispatch note
purpose: Turn an image of a short note into a page that can be printed or attached to an order.
step: Import the practice image as a scan. Set the crop so the title and last line stay inside the page.
check: Open the PDF and check that Dispatch note, Code A17 and Twelve notebooks are all visible.

title: Move a receipt ahead of its supporting pages
purpose: Lead with proof of dispatch without dropping the two supporting pages.
step: Drag the third thumbnail to the first position. Keep the packing list ahead of the instructions.
check: The receipt should now be page 1, with the packing list on page 2 and pickup instructions on page 3.

title: Mark a dispatch packet as a draft
purpose: Distinguish a review copy from the packet that can be sent to a driver.
step: Add the text DRAFT on all three pages. Choose a light enough opacity to read the underlying quantities.
check: Inspect the first and last pages. Both should carry DRAFT while the A17 and DEMO-482 references remain legible.

title: Trim excess margins from a scanned note
purpose: Bring the text closer to the page edges without cutting the scanned stock code.
step: Move the crop handles around the three lines. Leave some breathing room below Twelve notebooks.
check: Open the exported crop at normal zoom and verify that no letters are cut off. Cropping is for framing, not hiding secrets.

title: Fill in a dispatch handover contact
purpose: Replace the sample contact in an interactive form and save a copy for handover.
step: Select the Contact field and replace Demo operator with Shift lead. Save the completed form.
check: Reopen the result and confirm Shift lead is visible in the field. Keep this editable copy if more changes are expected.

title: Change an existing pickup time in a PDF
purpose: Correct a short time in an existing line of text while keeping the rest of the packet intact.
step: Open page 2, select the text containing 14:00 and change the start time to 15:00. Keep the replacement short enough to fit.
check: Reopen the saved PDF. Check that the end time stays 16:00 and that the revised start time appears in the right place.

title: Make a print copy of a Word stock table
purpose: Share a table with someone who needs its layout but does not need to edit the Word document.
step: Convert the sample DOCX directly and inspect the page containing Item and Quantity.
check: Read the header and all four data rows in the PDF. Check the page edge for clipped cells.

title: Bring a dispatch brief into an editable Word document
purpose: Reuse the wording of a dispatch packet in a document editor.
step: Choose text-based conversion for this digital PDF and export to DOCX. Check the reading order before revising the brief.
check: Find Pickup instructions in the Word file and change a copy of the time. Compare the remaining wording against the PDF.

title: Turn a three-page packet into briefing slides
purpose: Use the packet as a visual briefing without rebuilding every page by hand.
step: Choose a page-preserving conversion for the three source pages and export a PowerPoint file.
check: Open the deck and check that Packing list, Pickup instructions and Dispatch receipt are separate slides in order.

title: Extract a stock table from PDF into Excel
purpose: Turn aligned quantities on a digital PDF page into spreadsheet cells that can be checked and reused.
step: Select the table page and inspect the column boundaries. Separate the SKU, item and unit count before exporting.
check: In Excel, locate B04 and make sure its quantity is 8. The three source quantities add up to 25.

title: Prepare a dispatch PDF for an archive review
purpose: Create a candidate archival copy of a simple text document and retain the original for comparison.
step: Choose the available archival output and review the tool’s validation or limitation messages. Download the converted copy.
check: Compare all three pages and their text. If an archive requires a specific PDF/A profile, validate the file with that archive’s checker.

title: Replace the author in PDF document properties
purpose: Use a team name in the document properties of an outgoing copy.
step: Open the metadata editor and change the author from PDFPilot Example Studio to Dispatch team. Preserve the title Dispatch packet.
check: Open the saved file’s properties. Its author should have changed and its visible packing list should still be intact.

title: Duplicate the receipt page for two recipients
purpose: Print two copies of a receipt while printing the other packet pages once.
step: Select page 3 for duplication and add one copy after the original receipt.
check: The exported document should have four pages and finish with two copies of Dispatch receipt.

title: Make a JPEG copy of a PNG shelf label
purpose: Prepare an image for a catalog that accepts JPEG uploads.
step: Add the PNG label and choose JPEG as the output format. Inspect the background and text before downloading.
check: Open the resulting JPG and check that the A17 text and the gold circle remain clear.

title: Resize a shelf label to 300 pixels wide
purpose: Create a smaller catalog thumbnail from a 600 × 400 image.
step: Keep the aspect ratio and set the new width to 300 pixels. Inspect the dimensions before saving.
check: The thumbnail should measure 300 × 200 pixels. A round marker should remain circular.

title: Make a scanned dispatch note searchable
purpose: Add searchable text to a one-page image scan that initially has no selectable text.
step: Choose English as the source language and run OCR on the scan. Inspect the recognized text around the stock code.
check: Open the searchable output and find Twelve notebooks. Double-check A17 against the original scan.

title: Summarize the key points of a dispatch brief
purpose: Extract a short reading aid from a three-page digital packet.
step: Generate the summary, then look for the inventory, pickup and receipt information that matters to the next reader.
check: Check any time, quantity or reference in the summary against the source before using it in a handover.

title: Finalize a filled handover form for distribution
purpose: Preserve the displayed contact on a copy whose form field no longer needs editing.
step: Confirm that the Contact field reads Demo operator and flatten a copy of the form.
check: Reopen the result. Demo operator should remain visible while the Contact field is no longer interactive.

title: Insert a handover form before a dispatch receipt
purpose: Add an approval sheet to an existing packet without sending the form as a separate attachment.
step: Use the dispatch packet as the base. Insert the handover page after Pickup instructions and before Dispatch receipt.
check: The new four-page packet should show the form on page 3 and the receipt on page 4.

title: Compare two versions of a pickup window
purpose: Find a single changed time between two otherwise matching dispatch packets.
step: Select dispatch.pdf as the earlier copy and dispatch-revised.pdf as the newer one. Compare page 2 first.
check: The pickup start changed from 14:00 to 15:00. The finish time and the receipt reference should still match.

title: Password-protect a dispatch attachment
purpose: Require an opening password on a copy before sharing the packet.
step: Set a new password for the output. Keep it separately from the file and save an unprotected original for your own use.
check: Close the exported copy and reopen it. Confirm it prompts for the password and contains three pages after unlocking.

title: Remove a known opening password from a practice packet
purpose: Create a working copy of an encrypted packet whose opening password you already have.
step: Use the public practice password dispatch-demo to unlock the supplied file. Use only files you are allowed to access.
check: Close and reopen the result. It should show the three dispatch pages without asking for an opening password.

title: Crop a shelf label for a catalog card
purpose: Remove the outer margin of a product photo while keeping both its code and colored marker.
step: Drag a crop around the teal label, keeping the left-hand circle and the complete A17 text inside it.
check: Check the saved image edges. The cream margin should be reduced without cutting either identifying mark.

title: Turn a landscape label to portrait orientation
purpose: Rotate a single landscape label for a portrait slot.
step: Rotate the sample one quarter turn and leave mirroring off. Check the orientation before exporting.
check: The resulting image should have a portrait aspect ratio. Check the lettering to make sure it was rotated rather than mirrored.

title: Reduce a catalog label JPEG for upload
purpose: Prepare a leaner image for a product listing while keeping the product code readable.
step: Compare the source size with a lower-quality JPEG setting and zoom in on the white A17 text.
check: Choose a copy only if the size and legibility meet your needs. Small, already-compressed images may offer little saving.

title: Inspect the author tag on a product photo
purpose: Find the author information embedded in a JPEG before sending it to a catalog vendor.
step: Open the metadata view and locate the EXIF artist field of the practice image.
check: The author tag should read PDFPilot Demo. Inspect any exported clean copy separately before sharing it.

title: Read a stock code from a photographed note
purpose: Recover a short identifier and quantity from a raster image.
step: Choose English for the source and run recognition on the practice note. Compare the recognized lines with the image.
check: Check A17 character by character and verify that Twelve notebooks appears as words in the result.

title: Combine a Word stock table and its illustration
purpose: Assemble a Word handout whose table precedes its picture page.
step: Put the table document before the illustrated document and run the merge. Inspect the document boundary in Word.
check: Look for Table conversion sample before Embedded picture sample and confirm that the picture is present.

title: Print a plain-text pickup brief as PDF
purpose: Turn a short text note into a print attachment without copying it into a word processor.
step: Select the TXT file and convert it. Check the line breaks between the instructions and pickup window.
check: The resulting PDF should include carton A17 and the full 14:00 to 16:00 pickup window.

title: Print a Markdown dispatch checklist
purpose: Preserve the heading and list structure of a Markdown brief in a printable copy.
step: Convert the practice Markdown document and inspect the heading Before pickup and its two list items.
check: The PDF should display the list as instructions. Check that the bold pickup label reads correctly on the page.

title: Print a local dispatch page to PDF
purpose: Save an HTML handover note for someone who will read it offline.
step: Choose local HTML input and open the practice file. Check the print layout before saving as PDF.
check: Open the output offline and confirm that the Before pickup heading, two list entries and pickup window are visible.

title: Print a stock-count sheet from CSV
purpose: Turn a warehouse export into a small table for a clipboard.
step: Convert the CSV and check that the quoted item Pens, blue fits into one cell rather than two columns.
check: The PDF should contain three product rows. The quantities for A17, B04 and C21 should read 12, 8 and 5.

title: Print stock and zone worksheets from Excel
purpose: Share readable inventory sheets with a team that does not use Excel.
step: Select the Stock and Zones worksheets for conversion. Inspect the preview for the right sheet order and column widths.
check: Verify that the PDF contains both the stock quantities and the North-to-N1 shelf mapping.

title: Print a 4:3 briefing deck without changing its shape
purpose: Send a read-only copy of a presentation with a 4:3 page shape.
step: Convert the original PPTX and inspect the page with the sample image and the page with a table.
check: The exported pages should retain the slide proportions. Check the heading and the last table row for clipping.

title: Turn a stock CSV into XML records
purpose: Prepare an XML version of a three-row stock feed for a system that reads named fields.
step: Import the CSV, inspect how the headings map to element names and keep sku, item, units and zone separate.
check: Find the B04 record in the XML. Its item should include the comma in Pens, blue and its units should read 8.

title: Flatten repeating XML stock records into CSV
purpose: Read a small XML inventory in a spreadsheet without manually copying each record.
step: Inspect the repeated record elements in the preview and select the tabular layout that puts one stock item on each row.
check: Check that the output has three item rows. Pens, blue must stay in one field when the CSV is reopened.

title: Export a warehouse worksheet as XML
purpose: Create a feed from the Stock tab while leaving the lookup sheet out.
step: Select the Stock worksheet. Preview the mapping of sku, item, units and zone before saving the XML.
check: Find A17 and C21 in the result. N1 belongs to the separate Zones sheet and should not appear as a stock item.

title: Import an XML inventory into an Excel workbook
purpose: Review a machine-readable stock feed in a familiar spreadsheet.
step: Preview the records and choose a layout that places sku, item, units and zone in separate spreadsheet columns.
check: Open the XLSX and find item B04 on its own row. The comma in its name should remain inside one cell.

title: Make a shareable JPEG from a HEIC shelf photo
purpose: Provide a conventional JPEG to a recipient whose catalog viewer cannot open HEIC photos.
step: Open the HEIC practice image, convert it to JPG and compare the new picture with the source.
check: Verify that the result opens as JPEG and that the A17 label stays upright. Compare small text at normal zoom.

title: Convert a HEIC label to PNG for markup
purpose: Prepare an image from a HEIC source for a workflow that specifically needs PNG.
step: Convert the sample to PNG and inspect the image at full size before adding any annotations.
check: The output should be a PNG showing a teal panel and a gold marker. Keep the original HEIC for future edits.

title: Turn an SVG shelf marker into a printable PDF
purpose: Place a self-contained shelf marker on a PDF page for printing.
step: Use the supplied SVG, which contains a teal rectangle and an A17 label. Convert it and inspect the print preview.
check: Check the output proportions and the full right edge of the label before printing.

title: Add a sample watermark to a catalog image
purpose: Identify a demonstration photo before sending it to a reseller.
step: Add the text SAMPLE. Position it away from A17 so the product code remains visible.
check: Open the exported image and check that SAMPLE is present, legible and clear of the identifying code.

title: Export API-style stock records to a CSV
purpose: Hand a spreadsheet user three stock records delivered as a JSON array.
step: Convert the array and inspect the cells under sku and item. A comma inside a JSON string needs CSV quoting in the output.
check: Reopen the CSV in a spreadsheet. B04 should have the single item name Pens, blue rather than an extra column.

title: Turn product catalog rows into JSON objects
purpose: Send a small product table to a system that accepts an array of records.
step: Use the first CSV row as field names and convert the three records. Inspect the JSON value types before import.
check: Check that every object has sku, item, units and zone. Validate whether the receiving system expects unit counts as strings or numbers.

title: Open a stock API response as an Excel workbook
purpose: Prepare a human-readable workbook from an array of product records.
step: Select the JSON sample and create an XLSX. Compare the spreadsheet headers with the keys in the first object.
check: The workbook should have three data rows. The North record should pair SKU A17 with quantity 12.

title: Export stock worksheet rows for an API
purpose: Turn a worksheet into records that a developer can inspect before importing them.
step: Convert the workbook’s Stock data and compare the property names against its column headers.
check: Find the East record and verify SKU C21 and units 5. Inspect value types before submitting the JSON to another system.

title: Change a tab-delimited stock feed to CSV
purpose: Pass a tab-separated export to software that expects commas between fields.
step: Convert the TSV and inspect the row whose item name contains its own comma.
check: The CSV should quote Pens, blue as one field. Reopening it should produce four columns for that row.

title: Prepare a tab-delimited stock import
purpose: Create a tab-separated feed from a CSV containing a quoted comma.
step: Convert the inventory CSV and view the result in an editor that can show tabs.
check: There should be three field separators in each product row. Pens, blue should still be one item.

title: Open a tab-separated stock list in Excel
purpose: Build a workbook from a TSV without pasting all the fields into a single cell.
step: Select the TSV sample and convert it to a spreadsheet. Inspect the first row for the four field names.
check: The North, South and East zones should appear in their own column next to the three stock quantities.

title: Create a tab-delimited worksheet export
purpose: Prepare the Stock worksheet for a plain-text data exchange.
step: Convert the workbook to TSV and inspect the separation between sku, item, units and zone.
check: Check the row containing Pens, blue. Its comma is part of the item name and should still be present.

title: Turn a YAML stock list into JSON for review
purpose: Check the structure of a YAML sequence in a JSON-based tool.
step: Convert the three YAML list items and inspect the first and last objects in the resulting array.
check: Check that units remains numeric for the three stock records and that B04 remains text.

title: Turn a stock fixture into readable YAML
purpose: Give a reviewer a YAML version of a compact JSON test fixture.
step: Convert the example array and inspect the indentation of the entries beneath each list item.
check: The YAML should contain three records. The comma in the second item name should survive a conversion back to JSON.

title: Publish a Markdown pickup checklist as HTML
purpose: Turn a two-item checklist into semantic HTML that can be inserted into a site.
step: Convert the Markdown sample and inspect the generated heading, list and emphasis tags.
check: The list should contain two items, and the pickup window should remain in the paragraph after the list.

title: Recover a pickup checklist as Markdown
purpose: Move a short HTML brief into a Markdown documentation repository.
step: Convert the local file and inspect how its heading, two bullets and bold label are represented.
check: Render the Markdown once. Check that Before pickup is a subheading and that both actions remain in the list.

title: Extract readable instructions from an HTML brief
purpose: Send the wording of a local HTML brief to a plain-text destination.
step: Convert the file and inspect the order of its heading, list items and closing paragraph.
check: Check that the output contains the pickup window and no literal HTML tags around the instructions.

title: Turn a plain-text dispatch note into HTML
purpose: Create HTML from a note without typing tags around each paragraph.
step: Convert the TXT sample and inspect the HTML alongside the original text.
check: Render the result and verify that the blank line after Dispatch brief has not joined the heading and the first instruction into one word.

title: Encode a short dispatch label as Base64
purpose: Produce a known test string to check a data pipeline’s encoding settings.
step: In text mode enter exactly Dispatch A17, with no line break at the end. Encode the value and copy the result.
check: The Base64 value should be RGlzcGF0Y2ggQTE3. A different suffix can indicate an extra newline in the input.

title: Decode a Base64 training label back to text
purpose: Check whether a Base64 field contains the expected human-readable label.
step: Paste RGlzcGF0Y2ggQTE3 from the sample into the decoder and inspect the decoded text.
check: The output should read Dispatch A17 with one space. Compare the capital D and the stock code with the expected label.

title: Escape an ampersand in a URL query value
purpose: Keep an ampersand inside a search term from being interpreted as the start of another URL parameter.
step: Encode the component pens & paper by itself. Leave the surrounding URL out of the input.
check: The result should be pens%20%26%20paper. Decode it once to check that the two spaces and ampersand return.

title: Read a percent-encoded search term
purpose: Inspect the actual text stored in an encoded search parameter.
step: Decode the sample pens%20%26%20paper as a single URL component.
check: The readable term should be pens & paper. Keep the ampersand as data if you later rebuild the URL.

title: Pretty-print a compact inventory response
purpose: Read a one-line API fixture during a code review.
step: Paste the compact JSON and apply indentation. Compare the first sku and the last zone before and after formatting.
check: The result should still parse as an array of three objects. A17 and East should still refer to the same records as before.

title: Compact a JSON stock fixture for transport
purpose: Remove formatting whitespace from a JSON fixture while preserving spaces inside strings.
step: Minify the indented input and compare its character count with the original.
check: Parse the output and verify the second item is still Pens, blue with a space after the comma.

title: Find a trailing comma in a JSON fixture
purpose: Locate a deliberate syntax error before handing a fixture to another tool.
step: Validate the practice file, remove the extra comma immediately before the closing bracket, then validate again.
check: The initial input should fail. After removing that one comma it should parse as a one-record array containing A17.

title: Indent a compact XML stock feed
purpose: Make repeated records in a single-line feed easier to inspect.
step: Format the XML and follow the nesting from stock to record to sku.
check: There should still be three record elements, each with one sku. Compare the units for B04 with the source.

title: Compact an indented XML stock feed
purpose: Prepare a small transfer copy of a structured feed with whitespace between its elements.
step: Minify the practice XML. Inspect the value of the item element containing Pens, blue.
check: The three record elements should remain separate. Spaces inside the item text should remain readable.

title: Find a mismatched closing tag in an XML feed
purpose: Diagnose a deliberate tag mismatch with a short reproducible example.
step: Validate the XML, match the closing tag to the opening sku tag, then run the check again.
check: The first check should report malformed XML. The corrected document should retain the A17 value and validate as well-formed.

title: Normalize quoting in an inventory CSV
purpose: Prepare a consistent CSV while preserving the comma in a quoted product name.
step: Format the source, then open the result with a CSV reader to inspect the B04 row.
check: The formatted file should parse as a header and three product rows, each with four fields.

title: Trim padding and blank rows in a stock list
purpose: Clean a small import file that contains whitespace around values and a completely blank row.
step: Run the cleaner and inspect the row whose SKU originally had a space on either side.
check: The cleaned SKU should be A17. Check that the blank row is gone and all three product records remain.

title: Remove an exact duplicate inventory record
purpose: Deduplicate an appended stock export without treating different products as duplicates.
step: Run the duplicate-row tool on the four product rows. Inspect the repeated A17 entry.
check: The result should contain the header and three unique product rows. A17 should appear only once.

title: Extract SKU and unit counts from a larger CSV
purpose: Prepare a two-column handoff that omits internal item descriptions and zone names.
step: Select sku and units in that order. Exclude item and zone before exporting.
check: The header should have two fields, with A17 and 12 in the first data row.

title: Split an inventory CSV into two-row batches
purpose: Make small import batches for a system with a row limit.
step: Set two data rows per part and split the three-item sample. Inspect each output file separately.
check: One part should contain two products and the other one product. Check the headers before importing either file.

title: Append a restock file to an inventory CSV
purpose: Combine a main stock list and a later delivery that use the same four headers.
step: Select the inventory first and the restock file second. Confirm the column names match.
check: The merged output should contain four products and a single header. Look for D09, Tape and 6 in the appended row.

title: Extract only the zone lookup worksheet
purpose: Share shelf locations without distributing the stock quantities in the same workbook.
step: Select Zones by name and export that worksheet into its own workbook.
check: The output should include the North-to-N1 mapping without the Stock worksheet or its product quantities.

title: Combine stock and restock worksheets in one workbook
purpose: Keep several worksheets together while preserving separate stock, zone and restock lists.
step: Add both workbooks and inspect the sheet names before merging.
check: Open the result and locate Stock, Zones and Restock. D09 should still appear in the Restock data.

title: Extract inventory rows from SQL INSERT statements
purpose: Review SQL seed records in a spreadsheet without connecting to a database.
step: Convert the INSERT statements in the sample and compare the CSV header with the SQL column list.
check: The output should contain three rows of values. The quoted SQL text Pens, blue should occupy one CSV field.

title: Build SQL seed INSERT statements from a stock CSV
purpose: Prepare a SQL seed script from an inventory table for a developer to review.
step: Convert the CSV using stock as the destination table when the tool asks for a name. Inspect quoting in the generated statements.
check: Read the columns and values together and find the B04 item. Review the script in a test environment before executing it.

title: Turn SQL seed statements into JSON test records
purpose: Reuse values from a SQL seed script in a JSON fixture without running the SQL.
step: Open the practice statements and convert their column lists and values into JSON records.
check: Verify that there are three records with the original four fields and that the quoted product name stays intact.

title: Generate SQL INSERT statements from JSON stock records
purpose: Prepare reviewable seed data from a small API response.
step: Convert the array of objects and review the destination table name and the generated value order.
check: Check the statement for C21. The quantity value should correspond to the units column and the East value to zone.

title: Build an XML stock feed from JSON records
purpose: Prepare an XML counterpart of a JSON fixture for a system that consumes tagged records.
step: Convert the array and inspect how each record’s keys become XML elements.
check: Check the representation of B04 and make sure its item value and quantity have stayed together.

title: Make JSON records from an XML inventory
purpose: Create a JSON version of a repeated-record feed for application testing.
step: Convert the three XML records and inspect the JSON properties generated from sku, item, units and zone.
check: Verify the South record contains B04 and Pens, blue. Check value types before comparing against an API schema.

title: Prepare an XML feed from a YAML stock list
purpose: Present a YAML inventory to a reviewer who works with tagged XML records.
step: Convert the list and inspect how the item and zone fields are nested within each record.
check: Find all three SKUs in the XML and verify that each one stays associated with its original zone.

title: Make a YAML copy of an XML stock feed
purpose: Provide an editable text representation of an XML inventory for review.
step: Convert the feed and inspect the indentation of repeated stock records in YAML.
check: Find C21 and verify that Folder and East are within the same record. Check whether scalar types match your importer.

title: Make an inventory workbook from a quoted CSV
purpose: Give a warehouse reviewer a spreadsheet with each identifier and item in its own cell.
step: Convert the CSV to XLSX, then inspect the cell containing Pens, blue in the new workbook.
check: There should be four columns and three product rows. Confirm that B04 has quantity 8 rather than a shifted column.

title: Export the stock worksheet as a CSV feed
purpose: Prepare a flat stock file for a catalog import while preserving the original workbook.
step: Use the Stock sheet as the source. Check that the zone lookup sheet has not been appended as product records.
check: Open the CSV and count three product rows. Pens, blue should remain one field when parsed.

title: Inspect the header and payload of a training JWT
purpose: Read the fields of a deliberately unsigned practice token without sharing a live credential.
step: Paste or load the supplied token and review its decoded header and payload. The header uses alg none.
check: Find sub set to demo-reader and purpose set to training. Decoding those values does not establish authenticity.

title: Find a changed stock quantity in two JSON fixtures
purpose: Locate a single changed quantity between two snapshots of the same three records.
step: Use stock.json as the earlier version and restock.json as the later version. Inspect the change under the B04 record.
check: Only its units value should move from 8 to 11. The item name and the other two records stay the same.

title: Turn a stock CSV into a README table
purpose: Make an inventory table that can be pasted into a Markdown document.
step: Convert the CSV and paste the result into a Markdown preview. Inspect the header separator row.
check: The rendered table should have four columns and three product rows. Pens, blue should fit inside one cell.

title: Recover CSV stock records from a README table
purpose: Move a table back from documentation into a spreadsheet-friendly data file.
step: Convert the Markdown table and inspect the CSV output. The Markdown alignment separator is formatting, not inventory data.
check: Reopen the CSV and check that three products remain and that the separator row was not imported as a product.

title: Redact a reference code from a dispatch receipt
purpose: Share a receipt without exposing the practice code on its last page.
step: Mark the complete DEMO-482 reference on page 3, apply redaction and export a separate copy.
check: Reopen the exported PDF, inspect the marked area, and search or copy text to check that the code cannot be recovered from it.

title: Reuse a dispatch brief in a Markdown handbook
purpose: Move readable text from a digital PDF packet into a version-controlled handbook.
step: Select the packet, extract its content as Markdown and review the page sequence before committing it anywhere.
check: Look for Packing list, Pickup instructions and Dispatch receipt in order. Compare the pickup time with the source.

title: Add a visible signature to a handover sheet
purpose: Place a visible sign-off on a practice handover form.
step: Add your practice signature below the contact field, away from the existing name. Save a new copy.
check: Reopen the PDF and check the signature’s size and position. This exercise uses a visible mark, not certificate-based identity verification.

title: Adjust contrast on a catalog label
purpose: Make the stock code easier to read while preserving the identifying colors of the practice label.
step: Adjust the photo in small steps and compare the white A17 lettering and gold circle against the source.
check: Inspect the saved copy at normal size. Keep a version in which the lettering remains distinct from the teal background.

title: Make a captioned image for a training slide
purpose: Add a readable cue to a practice image for an onboarding slide.
step: Add the caption CHECK THE CODE. Move it so it does not cover A17, then export the image.
check: View the result at slide size. Both the caption and the product code should be readable.

title: Blur a face in a training illustration
purpose: Practice obscuring a face before editing a group photo. The example is an illustration rather than a photograph of a person.
step: Mark the face manually so the region covers the eyes, nose and mouth. Inspect the blur before exporting.
check: Review the exported image itself at full size. The marked area should cover the whole target and leave the surrounding background alone.

title: Save a dispatch HTML card as a PNG
purpose: Create a static image of a local HTML handover note for a message or presentation.
step: Select the practice HTML file, preview the layout and choose PNG. Adjust the capture size to include the final paragraph.
check: Open the image and check both list items and the full pickup window. A clipped last line indicates the capture needs more height.

title: Remove a solid background from a shelf label
purpose: Isolate a rectangular label on a uniform cream background for use on different layouts.
step: Select the cream background and adjust the removal until the teal label’s outer shape stays intact. Export with transparency.
check: Place the PNG on a contrasting background to inspect its edges. Check the gold circle and white A17 lettering are preserved.

title: Enlarge a small product label for a slide
purpose: Increase the pixel dimensions of a 600 × 400 label while keeping its 3:2 shape.
step: Choose a 2× enlargement and inspect the lettering in the preview before saving.
check: Confirm the exported image measures 1200 × 800. Inspect the A17 text at 100% to judge whether it suits the slide.

title: Translate a dispatch brief and verify its times
purpose: Make a reading copy in another language while protecting the meaning of times and stock identifiers.
step: Open the English packet in a desktop browser offering the required translation language pair. Select the destination language and review page 2.
check: Compare A17, DEMO-482 and 14:00 to 16:00 with the original. Keep the source alongside the translated copy for checking.
